description: Northern Thai lantern: a ribbed cloth-over-bamboo drum with a scalloped skirt, hung at temples and during Yi Peng

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Hanging lantern built as a tall drum of stretched cloth over a frame, its sides bulging gently and divided by raised vertical ribs into broad panels, a flat circular cap closing the top with a short stiff hanging loop standing up from it, a narrow band collar around the drum at the bottom, and below that a short stiff skirt of wide scalloped tabs standing out in a ring, each tab a solid tapered flap rather than a loose strand Materials: Ivory and gold cloth with a saffron-yellow band, the weave visible and the colour sun-faded and blotched with damp on one side, gold foil trim on the ribs and collar rubbed thin, dust and cobwebs along the top cap, the skirt tabs creased and dog-eared.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93 carried from the recorded review; the rope added 472 triangles and one material. 2344/4000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: Measured bbox 0.441 x 1.016 x 0.441 m against the declared 0.42 x 1.02 x 0.42 -- the height re-declared from 0.72 to 1.02 on the owner's brief (2026-09-03) because the prop now ships WITH a 0.30 m hanging cord; the fixture itself is unchanged at 0.72 and sits at y -1.02..-0.30 under the loop's crown at the origin. Width and depth 5% over, the overshoot being the skirt's pleat amplitude.

A stiff twenty-pleat fan at 30 mm amplitude over a profile that flares to r 0.214 and turns back up at the hem, hanging directly off the drum's foot band. Unchanged; shifted down 0.30 with the fixture.
Twenty ribs running the drum's full height as a modulation around the axis, tinted toward a darker cream at the troughs. Unchanged.

Three material layers now: cream cloth at luma 186 carrying its rib troughs as a vertex colour, gilt trim at luma 150 for the cap, the three gathering bands and the new eyelet, and a JUTE ROPE material (#b09f7c, the canopy bay's probed rope tone) with a 256 px laid-strand tile on culm UVs so the strands run along the cord and round the loop. The 4 mm gold wire stub the plate showed is replaced by the cord the owner asked for; it rises from a gold eyelet on the cap through a whipped knot to a loop of r 0.023 whose crown is the origin.
featureReviews.notes: The cord is an owner addition the plate does not show (it hangs on a bare wire there); tone carried from a probed sibling rather than measured on this plate.

name: Lanna Cloth Hanging Lantern
notes:
The northern Thai temple lantern (โคมล้านนา), hung in ranks along temple eaves and through Chiang Mai during Yi Peng -- distinct from the round red Chinese lantern in that it is a tall ribbed drum with a stiff scalloped skirt rather than a plump barrel with a tassel. Sized as a 0.42 m drum with the skirt bringing the fixture to 0.72 m, plus a 0.30 m jute hanging cord with a loop (owner request 2026-09-03: the cord ships WITH the prop so it can hang from things), so the declared height is 1.02. The origin is the crown of the loop -- top-center, the hanging point -- and the fixture occupies y -1.02 to -0.30. The skirt is authored as a ring of solid tapered tabs rather than a fringe deliberately: fringed geometry is what the reference reconstruction loses and what costs a low-end GPU its frame. Static: hung, so physics stays disabled.

BUDGET CLASS RAISED medium -> large (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.
